head: Cloud identification app Cielo names cloud types from your camera
dek: Cielo, a $3.99 iPhone and iPad app, estimates which type of cloud is in the sky from your live camera, a photo or a saved video. It was #35 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 25 November.
details: It shows the main cloud type, how confident it is, other possible types and a rough estimate of how much of the sky is covered. Analysis runs on the Cielo service, so it needs an internet connection; for videos only sampled still images are sent, not the file or its sound. The listing says glare, haze and mixed skies can affect results and that it isn't a forecast. The maker is Richard Podolsky; it's out since 13 October.
where: iPhone and iPad (iOS 15.1 or later), $3.99, internet needed
means: If you've wondered what kind of clouds you're looking at, it gives an estimate in seconds, but it's not for weather or flying decisions.
todo: Read the App Store listing before buying; it has no ratings yet.
